clue.text: "Pulp" featured in this newly remixed chart-topper

indicators.note: a thing featured in something appears inside it, so one piece sits within the other
a track newly remixed has its parts rearranged, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: to pulp something is to mash it

explanation.surface: A Britpop band's song has been remixed and gone to number one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulp' reads as the Britpop band, a natural thing to feature in a chart-topper, but it is simply a verb meaning to crush; 'newly remixed' splits the reshuffled letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A big hit record is one that tops the charts; the phrase is the usual label for a runaway success.

clue.text: Winter vehicle presently parking in Berkshire town

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: Slough is a town in the English county of Berkshire, west of London
presently means now, at the present time
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A winter vehicle is currently parked in a Berkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for clearing snow from roads is a vehicle used chiefly in winter.

clue.text: Principled Greek Olympian's agreed to interrupt

indicators.note: the piece that interrupts breaks into the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: Ares, the Greek god of war, is one of the Olympian gods
to chime is to agree, as in chime with

explanation.surface: A Greek of high principles agreed to interrupt an Olympic athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principled' alludes to Archimedes' principle about floating bodies, not to moral principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was the Greek mathematician known for the principle of buoyancy, hence a Greek with a principle.

clue.text: Frequent adviser offering tip with a chance of success?

indicators.note: a chance of success puts one in the hunt, so with it means placed inside

parts.note: to be in the hunt is to have a chance of winning

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An agony columnist offers a tip that might help you succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the hunt' means having a chance of success, so A, the tip of 'adviser', goes inside HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to visit it often, the verb sense of haunting somewhere.

clue.text: New to CBS TV show, serial killer admits mass 13s approach!

indicators.note: something that admits another lets it in, so it goes inside
a new version of something is a remade form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A serial killer appears in a new show on American television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TO CBS TV SHOW SERIAL KILLER and 'admits' adds M. The answer is a regional English saying for an approaching storm; 13 is STORM CLOUD.
explanation.definitionFit: This English regional saying is uttered when dark storm clouds are gathering and rain is about to fall.

clue.text: Not a catering school, this measure of hard knocks?

indicators.note: to school is to train or drill, knocking raw material into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: This isn't a catering college: it trains people for life's hard knocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is the anagram signal on NOT A CATERING. The 'hard knocks' are engine knocking, which a fuel's grade is rated to resist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuel's anti-knock grade tells how well it resists premature ignition, the knocking in an engine.

clue.text: Whip arrests MP somewhere in Normandy

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: cat is short for cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A party whip arrests a Member of Parliament somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests the parliamentary enforcer, which suits MP; here it is the CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a village in Normandy that gives its name to the famous soft cheese.

clue.text: Objection lodged on American border

indicators.note: in a down clue, lodged on means placed below, so it comes after

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no buts

explanation.surface: An objection is raised about an American border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a noun but is the verb: to adjoin.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin or share an edge with something, which is what bordering it means.

clue.text: My point is often hidden from life peers

indicators.note: the letters come from within the words, read straight through

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their argument often gets lost on members of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the sword itself: a fencing épée's point is usually covered by a button.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencing sword's tip is normally blunted and capped with a button so that it cannot wound.

clue.text: Naturally lost: abstract female

indicators.note: to abstract is to draw out or remove, so the letter for female is taken away

parts.note: someone lost has strayed from their route, off course

explanation.surface: A woman lost in abstract thought, behaving as naturally as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' looks like an adjective describing the female, but it is a verb meaning remove: one F goes from OFF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in reply, the phrase means certainly or as you would expect, the same as naturally.

clue.text: Dodgy tum my nemesis?

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound or out of order, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone with a weak stomach complains that it is their constant enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges TUM MY NEMESIS; the whole clue also hints at the body's defences, whose foe is the bug behind an upset tum.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's disease-fighting network is the natural enemy of whatever infection upsets a stomach.

clue.text: See 4
Leaving home at one, southern Englishman acquired painting

indicators.note: the Englishman acquires, or takes in, the other letters, so they go inside him

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person
someone leaving home at one o'clock stays in till one: IN TILL I, with I as the numeral one

explanation.surface: A southern Englishman who left home at one o'clock picked up a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'southern Englishman' looks like one unit, but S belongs to the inserted piece: IN TILL I plus S goes inside POM, as 'acquired' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointillism is a style of painting built from small dots of colour, as practised by Seurat.

clue.text: Warning issued from slur.com?

indicators.note: what issues from something emerges in a new form, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a web address is read aloud with dot for the full stop: slur dot com

explanation.surface: A warning has been posted from a website devoted to slurs.
explanation.walkthrough: The '.' must be spelt as DOT for the letters of SLUR DOT COM to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark clouds gathering are a sign that bad weather is coming, so they serve as a warning.

clue.text: Lie up, as medicine man looking down on soldiers besieging Villa?

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece looking down on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: besiegers surround a place, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
Pancho Villa was the Mexican revolutionary general

explanation.surface: A doctor looking down on troops laying siege to a villa, as they lie low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Villa' looks like a house or Aston Villa football club; it is Pancho Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lies up stays moored in one place, which is what lowering its anchor does.

clue.text: Lines about film venue

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a set of lines
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Some writing about where a film is being shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a well-known British chain of cinemas, and the name has become a byword for a picture house.

clue.text: The right change?

parts.note: plays on the saying right as ..., meaning perfectly fine, and on change as small coins

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper asks whether this is the correct change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right as ninepence' is an old British phrase for perfectly well; ninepence was a sum in pre-decimal coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British saying right as ninepence makes this sum of small coins the proverbially right amount.

clue.text: Pass reader a squirrel

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lector is a reader, in church or at a university

explanation.surface: Someone hands a reader a squirrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a squirrel' is the definition in its figurative sense: someone who hoards things away, as a squirrel stores nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel, figuratively, is a hoarder who stores things away, just like someone who amasses objects.

clue.text: Where actor may be found, never turning into a married man

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a groom is a man just married

indicators.note: turning means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: An actor, never turning into a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never' is shortened to its poetic form before 'turning' acts on it; the reversed letters sit just after the first letter of the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The green room is the backstage lounge where performers wait before going on.

clue.text: Fruit of Borneo one put in mouth

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, as in shut your trap
a is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit from Borneo being popped into someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarap is a large spiky fruit related to the breadfruit, grown in Borneo.

clue.text: Up to no good with Eric, ran from Caribbean island

indicators.note: up to no good suggests mischief, and these letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Eric was up to mischief, so he fled from a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to no good' reads as a phrase, but 'Up to' is fodder and 'no good' the anagram signal over UP TO, ERIC and RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Puerto Rico, the Caribbean island, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: He had a tale to tell about the First Lady

definitions.text: He had a tale to tell

parts.note: re means about, as in business letters
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man has a story to tell about the US President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests the White House; it is Eve. The Reeve is a Chaucer pilgrim who tells a tale in The Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reeve, an estate manager, is a pilgrim in Chaucer who tells The Reeve's Tale.

clue.text: "Love is Tender", heading for the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading for the top means read upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: tender means sore, painful to the touch

explanation.surface: A song title about tender love is headed for the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the definition: Eros is the Greek god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of desire, standing for love itself.

clue.text: I can confirm the end of inflammatory condition

definitions.meaning: a reply that confirms something: yes, that is so
the medical suffix for inflammation, as in tonsillitis

explanation.walkthrough: The suffix for inflammation ends words like appendicitis and arthritis.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words meaning that's so also spell the suffix doctors use for an inflammatory illness.

clue.text: See 5
What has me pinned back by the two large animals? One only

indicators.note: something pinned is held fast between two others, so it sits inside
pinned by the pair means hemmed in by them, placed within

parts.note: both means the two together
eh is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone is pinned down by two big beasts, then told it was just one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' is the questioning interjection said when you mishear. The definition plays on the Hebrew name, which looks plural yet names one creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical beast in Job has a name that looks plural in Hebrew yet denotes one enormous animal.

clue.text: See 10
Part of letter read out by a man in Post Office?

indicators.note: words read out are spoken, so the answer is said like the phrase

parts.note: a person at the post office handing in mail is a sender

explanation.surface: Someone at the post office is having a letter read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' seems to be mail, but it is an alphabet letter: an ascender is the stroke rising above the line, as in b or d.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography the stroke of a lower-case letter rising above the x-height, as in h or k, has this name.
